uutiset.t: Deutsche Bank Seeks to Curb Fallout From Data Leaks
uutiset.s: Deutsche Bank sought to contain the fallout from a data leak which provided new details of payments tied to Jeffrey Epstein and efforts to expand its Russian business prior to the full scale invasion of Ukraine. Alex Morgan explains. (Source: Bloomberg)

uutiset.t: Disney Profit Beats With Marvel Films Powering Streaming
uutiset.s: Walt Disney reported sales and earnings that exceeded analysts’ expectations, with a particularly strong result in its streaming TV unit. Operating income in business that include the Disney+ and Hulu streaming services doubled to $824 million in the fiscal fourth quarter, due to higher subscription

uutiset.t: Mark Walter’s Largest Insurer Sees Sales Plunge After US Probe
uutiset.s: Annuity sales at billionaire Los Angeles Dodgers owner Mark Walter’s largest insurance company dropped after a federal investigation into the firm’s accounting practices became public.

uutiset.t: Bank of America Says US Rates Will Rise ‘Until Activity Cools’
uutiset.s: US short-term interest rates are likely to continue to rise in the absence of signs that they are restraining the American economy, according to interest-rate strategists at Bank of America Corp.

uutiset.t: Sellas Life Sciences Stock Triples After Cancer Vaccine Data
uutiset.s: Sellas Life Sciences Group Inc. surged after the drug developer reported positive late-stage trial results for an experimental cancer vaccine to treat an aggressive form of blood cancer.

uutiset.t: Wall Street Awaits First Nvidia Earnings Report Without Jensen Huang
uutiset.s: Jonathan Ferro, Lisa Abramowicz and Annmarie Hordern speak daily with leaders and decision makers from Wall Street to Washington and beyond. No other program better positions investors and executives for the trading day than "Bloomberg Surveillance." (Source: Bloomberg)

uutiset.t: Treasuries Rise as Risk-Averse Investors Dump Stocks, Buy Bonds
uutiset.s: Treasuries gained as investors, alarmed by the latest in a series of technology breakdowns over the past week, flocked to US government bonds as a haven from stocks.

uutiset.t: Optimum Nears Deal With Creditors to Slash $26 Billion Debt Pile
uutiset.s: Optimum Communications Inc. and its creditors are in advanced talks over how much of its roughly $26 billion debt pile to cut as part of the troubled telecommunications firm’s broader reorganization.

uutiset.t: Nuclear Thriller Puts Spotlight on French Election Campaign
uutiset.s: France is about to elect a new president with the power to launch a nuclear strike. The new film Jupiter imagines what happens next.

uutiset.t: Lucky Strike Shares Jump 22% as CEO Makes Take-Private Offer
uutiset.s: Shares of Lucky Strike Entertainment Corp. soared 22% after founder Thomas Shannon proposed taking the company private following a bruising stretch in which its stock hit a record low and its debt fell into distressed territory.

uutiset.t: SpaceX Debt for AI Chips to Hit Market as Soon as This Week
uutiset.s: SpaceX may kick off part of a $40 billion debt sale to fund its purchase of artificial intelligence chips as soon as this week, according to people with knowledge of the matter.

uutiset.t: Saks, Neiman Marcus Parent Company CEO Says Growth Plan Is on Track
uutiset.s: Exemplar Luxury Group CEO Geoffroy van Raemdonck says the Saks Fifth Avenue and Neiman Marcus parent company is profitable and aims to grow revenue from $7 billion to $9 billion. uutiset.t: Tech Stocks Sink Before Nvidia’s First Results After Huang Exit
uutiset.s: US stocks slumped for a fourth day as investors looked to an all-important earnings release from Nvidia Corp. after the market close to potentially help restore confidence in the artificial-intelligence trade.

uutiset.t: Swiss Pharma Employee Convicted Over $300,000 Insider Trades
uutiset.s: An employee of Swiss healthcare supplier SKAN Group AG was found guilty of insider trading after his appeal of a penalty order handed down by Swiss prosecutors was rejected.

uutiset.t: European Stocks Extend Fall as Tech Drags; Deutsche Bank Slides
uutiset.s: European stocks extended declines Tuesday, weighed down by technology stocks ahead of results from Nvidia Corp.
